note: Machine-readable inventory of everything this fork adds on top of upstream. Drives `bun run fork:verify` (run after every sync to prove nothing was silently dropped) and `bun run sync:check` (detect when upstream has moved past our baseline). Update `baseline` after each successful sync. Keep the human-readable rationale in FORK_WORKFLOW.md in step with this file.

baseline.comment: Last upstream commit fully merged into dev. sync:check compares upstream/dev against this ref. Bump it (and forkTag) after every sync.

patched.note: Registers all fork CLI commands via a single .command(ForkCommands). The upstream command block must stay byte-identical to upstream.
In-app updater points at the fork (releaseRepo/installUrl/npm/brew), never upstream, so an update prompt cannot clobber our binary.
Multi-select discovered local providers; graceful mDNS failure.
Unified context bar, % inline, breakdown below; Context label; cost for cloud providers.

createEffect writing ThemeState.set(store.active) — the writer half of the local-backend themed-loading-screen feature (reader is provider.ts ThemeState.get). theme-state.ts now lives in packages/core/src/local so both the TUI (writer) and the opencode provider (reader) can share the singleton across the package boundary.
Fork services joined to upstream's LayerNode graph: BeadsSync, AutoMode, LocalProviderSync, Loop, SideQuestion. Loop/SideQuestion own HTTP routes and publish events, so they must be in the graph.

Appends fork-owned event definitions (loop.updated, side-question.response) to the shared schema manifest. Their schemas live in packages/opencode and cannot be declared in packages/schema, and without this they are absent from the generated Event union so no client can subscribe.

Compaction that itself overflows retries with only the most recent user turn, then falls back to a minimal summary, instead of returning "stop" and stranding the session. Silently lost in the 0d927ba03f merge and only noticed because a fork-only test still asserted it.
Pins LC_ALL=C on git spawns. This code matches git's human-readable output by text (forceRequired), and git localises it — on a non-English machine those checks silently read false.
